record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity in near-Chebyshev single-valuedness
record.original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b> for b in U. For a nonempty closed subset C of U, let P_left,C(y) be the set of points in C minimizing D(., y). Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. If f is additionally supercoercive, then P_left,C is known to be single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is the supercoercivity assumption genuinely necessary for this almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness conclusion?

evidence.quote: Fact 3.5 (See [7, Corollary 5.6].) Suppose that f is supercoercive, that f is twice continuously differentiable, and that for every y in U, grad^2 f(y) is positive definite. Then <-PC is almost everywhere and generically single-valued on U.
It would be interesting to see whether or not supercoercivity is essential in Fact 3.5.
Problem 5. Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 3.5 really essential?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \mathbb{R}^n$ and let $f: X \to [-\infty, +\infty]$ be a convex function of Legendre type (i.e., essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex). Set $U = \operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom} f)$, and define the Bregman distance
$$D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - \langle \nabla f(b), a - b \rangle \quad \text{for } a \in X,\ b \in U.$$
For a nonempty closed subset $C \subseteq U$, define the left Bregman projection
$$P_{\leftarrow, C}(y) = \operatorname*{argmin}_{c \in C} D(c, y), \quad y \in U.$$
Assume in addition that $f$ is twice continuously differentiable on $U$ and that the Hessian $\nabla^2 f(y)$ is positive definite for every $y \in U$. It is known that if $f$ is moreover supercoercive (i.e., $\lim_{\|x\| \to \infty} f(x)/\|x\| = +\infty$), then $P_{\leftarrow, C}$ is single-valued both Lebesgue-almost everywhere and on a generic (dense $G_\delta$) subset of $U$.

Question: Is the supercoercivity hypothesis on $f$ genuinely necessary for the conclusion that $P_{\leftarrow, C}$ is almost everywhere and generically single-valued on $U$? Equivalently, does there exist a convex Legendre function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, twice continuously differentiable with positive definite Hessian on $U$ but not supercoercive, together with a nonempty closed subset $C \subseteq U$, for which $P_{\leftarrow, C}$ fails to be single-valued almost everywhere or generically on $U$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related work on Bregman distances, Chebyshev sets, and supercoercivity (including surveys, generalized Bregman envelopes, and BPG algorithm relaxations of supercoercivity), but no source explicitly resolves whether the supercoercivity assumption is essential for the almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness of the left Bregman projection in this setting. The status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Bregman distances and Chebyshev sets
status_evidence.snippet: Original framework establishing the almost everywhere and generic single-valuedness under supercoercivity (Corollary 5.6).
status_evidence.claim: Provides the baseline result whose necessity of supercoercivity is being questioned.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Bregman Envelopes and Proximity Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for convexity, coercivity, and supercoercivity for generalized Bregman distances are furnished.
status_evidence.claim: Related developments discuss supercoercivity but do not resolve necessity in the Chebyshev-single-valuedness problem.

status_evidence.title: The Generalized Bregman Distance
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generalized Bregman distances without addressing whether supercoercivity is essential for generic/a.e. single-valuedness of left Bregman projections.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the necessity question.
